28type BaseType = super::BitFieldBaseType;
29const BASE_BITS: usize = super::BIT_FIELD_BASE_BITS;
30const BASE_SHIFT: usize = super::BIT_FIELD_SHIFT_BITS;
31
32/**
33 * <p>Represents a 2D matrix of bits. In function arguments below, and throughout the common
34 * module, x is the column position, and y is the row position. The ordering is always x, y.
35 * The origin is at the top-left.</p>
36 *
37 * <p>Internally the bits are represented in a 1-D array of 32-bit ints. However, each row begins
38 * with a new int. This is done intentionally so that we can copy out a row into a BitArray very
39 * efficiently.</p>
40 *
41 * <p>The ordering of bits is row-major. Within each int, the least significant bits are used first,
42 * meaning they represent lower x values. This is compatible with BitArray's implementation.</p>
43 *
44 * @author Sean Owen
45 * @author dswitkin@google.com (Daniel Switkin)
46 */
47#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
48pub struct BitMatrix {
49    width: u32,
50    height: u32,
51    row_size: usize,
52    bits: Vec<BaseType>,
53}
54
55impl BitMatrix {
56    /**
57     * Creates an empty square {@code BitMatrix}.
58     *
59     * @param dimension height and width
60     */
61    pub fn with_single_dimension(dimension: u32) -> Result<Self> {
62        Self::new(dimension, dimension)
63    }

65    /**
66     * Creates an empty {@code BitMatrix}.
67     *
68     * @param width bit matrix width
69     * @param height bit matrix height
70     */
71    pub fn new(width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<Self> {
72        if width < 1 || height < 1 {
73            return Err(Exceptions::illegal_argument_with(
74                "Both dimensions must be greater than 0",
75            ));
76        }
77        Ok(Self {
78            width,
79            height,
80            row_size: (width as usize).div_ceil(BASE_BITS),
81            bits: vec![0; (width as usize).div_ceil(BASE_BITS) * height as usize],
82        })
83        // this.width = width;
84        // this.height = height;
85        // this.rowSize = (width + 31) / 32;
86        // bits = new int[rowSize * height];
87    }

105    /**
106     * Interprets a 2D array of booleans as a {@code BitMatrix}, where "true" means an "on" bit.
107     *
108     * @param image bits of the image, as a row-major 2D array. Elements are arrays representing rows
109     * @return {@code BitMatrix} representation of image
110     */
111    pub fn parse_bools(image: &[Vec<bool>]) -> Self {
112        let height: u32 = image.len().try_into().unwrap();
113        let width: u32 = image[0].len().try_into().unwrap();
114        let mut bits = BitMatrix::new(width, height).unwrap();
115        for (i, imageI) in image.iter().enumerate().take(height as usize) {
116            // for i in 0..height as usize {
117            //for (int i = 0; i < height; i++) {
118            // let imageI = &image[i];
119            for (j, imageI_j) in imageI.iter().enumerate().take(width as usize) {
120                // for j in 0..width as usize {
121                //for (int j = 0; j < width; j++) {
122                if *imageI_j {
123                    bits.set(j as u32, i as u32);
124                }
125            }
126        }
127        bits
128    }
129
130    pub fn parse_strings(
131        string_representation: &str,
132        set_string: &str,
133        unset_string: &str,
134    ) -> Result<Self> {
135        // cannot pass nulls in rust
136        // if (stringRepresentation == null) {
137        //   throw new IllegalArgumentException();
138        // }
139
140        let mut bits = vec![false; string_representation.chars().count()];
141        let mut bitsPos = 0;
142        let mut rowStartPos = 0;
143        let mut rowLength = 0; //-1;
144        let mut first_run = true;
145        let mut nRows = 0;
146        let mut pos = 0;
147        let chars: Vec<char> = string_representation.chars().collect();
148        while pos < chars.len() {
149            if chars.get(pos).ok_or(Exceptions::ILLEGAL_STATE)? == &'\n'
150                || chars.get(pos).ok_or(Exceptions::ILLEGAL_STATE)? == &'\r'
151            {
152                if bitsPos > rowStartPos {
153                    //if rowLength == -1 {
154                    if first_run {
155                        first_run = false;
156                        rowLength = bitsPos - rowStartPos;
157                    } else if bitsPos - rowStartPos != rowLength {
158                        return Err(Exceptions::illegal_argument_with(
159                            "row lengths do not match",
160                        ));
161                    }
162                    rowStartPos = bitsPos;
163                    nRows += 1;
164                }
165                pos += 1;
166            } else if string_representation[pos..].starts_with(set_string) {
167                pos += set_string.len();
168                bits[bitsPos] = true;
169                bitsPos += 1;
170            } else if string_representation[pos..].starts_with(unset_string) {
171                pos += unset_string.len();
172                bits[bitsPos] = false;
173                bitsPos += 1;
174            } else {
175                return Err(Exceptions::illegal_argument_with(format!(
176                    "illegal character encountered: {}",
177                    string_representation[pos..].to_owned()
178                )));
179            }
180        }
181
182        // no EOL at end?
183        if bitsPos > rowStartPos {
184            //if rowLength == -1 {
185            if first_run {
186                // first_run = false;
187                rowLength = bitsPos - rowStartPos;
188            } else if bitsPos - rowStartPos != rowLength {
189                return Err(Exceptions::illegal_argument_with(
190                    "row lengths do not match",
191                ));
192            }
193            nRows += 1;
194        }
195
196        let mut matrix = BitMatrix::new(rowLength as u32, nRows)?;
197        for (i, bit) in bits.iter().enumerate().take(bitsPos) {
198            // for i in 0..bitsPos {
199            //for (int i = 0; i < bitsPos; i++) {
200            if *bit {
201                matrix.set((i % rowLength) as u32, (i / rowLength) as u32);
202            }
203        }
204        Ok(matrix)
205    }

207    /**
208     * Gets the requested bit, where true means black.
209     *
210     * x The horizontal component (i.e. which column)
211     * y The vertical component (i.e. which row)
212     * returns the value of given bit in matrix, or false if the requested point is out of bounds of the image
213     */
214    #[inline(always)]
215    pub fn get(&self, x: u32, y: u32) -> bool {
216        let offset = self.get_offset(y, x);
217        if offset >= self.bits.len() {
218            return false;
219        }
220        ((self.bits[offset] >> (x as usize & BASE_SHIFT)) & 1) != 0
221    }
222
223    #[inline(always)]
224    pub fn get_point(&self, point: Point) -> bool {
225        self.get(point.x as u32, point.y as u32)
226        // let offset = self.get_offset(point.y as u32, point.x as u32);
227        // ((self.bits[offset] >> (x & BASE_SHIFT)) & 1) != 0
228    }

230    #[inline(always)]
231    pub fn get_index<T: Into<usize>>(&self, index: T) -> bool {
232        self.get_point(self.calculate_pointrom_index(index.into()))
233    }
234
235    #[inline(always)]
236    fn calculate_pointrom_index(&self, index: usize) -> Point {
237        let row = index / (self.getWidth() as usize);
238        let column = index % (self.getWidth() as usize);
239        point_i(column as u32, row as u32)
240    }
241
242    #[inline(always)]
243    fn get_offset(&self, y: u32, x: u32) -> usize {
244        y as usize * self.row_size + (x as usize / BASE_BITS)
245    }
246
247    pub fn try_get(&self, x: u32, y: u32) -> Option<bool> {
248        let offset = self.get_offset(y, x);
249        if offset >= self.bits.len() {
250            return None;
251        }
252        Some(((self.bits[offset] >> (x as usize & BASE_SHIFT)) & 1) != 0)
253    }
254
255    #[inline(always)]
256    pub fn try_get_point(&self, point: Point) -> Option<bool> {
257        self.try_get(point.x as u32, point.y as u32)
258    }

260    pub fn try_get_area(&self, x: u32, y: u32, box_size: u32) -> Option<bool> {
261        let mut matrix = Vec::with_capacity((box_size * box_size) as usize);
262        let start_x = (x as i32 - box_size as i32 / 2).max(0) as u32;
263        let end_x = x + box_size / 2;
264        let start_y = (y as i32 - box_size as i32 / 2).max(0) as u32;
265        let end_y = y + box_size / 2;
266
267        for get_x in start_x..=end_x {
268            for get_y in start_y..=end_y {
269                matrix.push(self.try_get(get_x, get_y)?);
270            }
271        }
272
273        let total_set = matrix.iter().filter(|bit| **bit).count();
274        if (total_set as f32 / matrix.len() as f32) >= 0.5 {
275            Some(true)
276        } else {
277            Some(false)
278        }
279    }

282    #[inline(always)]
283    pub fn check_in_bounds(&self, x: u32, y: u32) -> bool {
284        (self.get_offset(y, x)) >= self.bits.len()
285    }

293    /**
294     * <p>Sets the given bit to true.</p>
295     *
296     * @param x The horizontal component (i.e. which column)
297     * @param y The vertical component (i.e. which row)
298     */
299    #[inline(always)]
300    pub fn set(&mut self, x: u32, y: u32) {
301        let offset = self.get_offset(y, x);
302        self.bits[offset] |= 1 << (x as usize & BASE_SHIFT);
303    }
304
305    #[inline(always)]
306    pub fn set_bool(&mut self, x: u32, y: u32, value: bool) {
307        if value {
308            self.set(x, y)
309        } else {
310            self.unset(x, y)
311        }
312    }
313
314    #[inline(always)]
315    pub fn unset(&mut self, x: u32, y: u32) {
316        let offset = self.get_offset(y, x);
317        self.bits[offset] &= !(1 << (x as usize & BASE_SHIFT));
318    }
319
320    /**
321     * <p>Flips the given bit.</p>
322     *
323     * @param x The horizontal component (i.e. which column)
324     * @param y The vertical component (i.e. which row)
325     */
326    #[inline(always)]
327    pub fn flip_coords(&mut self, x: u32, y: u32) {
328        let offset = self.get_offset(y, x);
329        self.bits[offset] ^= 1 << (x as usize & BASE_SHIFT);
330    }
331
332    /**
333     * <p>Flips every bit in the matrix.</p>
334     */
335    pub fn flip_self(&mut self) {
336        let max = self.bits.len();
337        for bit_set in self.bits.iter_mut().take(max) {
338            *bit_set = !*bit_set;
339        }
340    }
341
342    /**
343     * Exclusive-or (XOR): Flip the bit in this {@code BitMatrix} if the corresponding
344     * mask bit is set.
345     *
346     * @param mask XOR mask
347     */
348    pub fn xor(&mut self, mask: &BitMatrix) -> Result<()> {
349        if self.width != mask.width || self.height != mask.height || self.row_size != mask.row_size
350        {
351            return Err(Exceptions::illegal_argument_with(
352                "input matrix dimensions do not match",
353            ));
354        }
355        // let mut rowArray = BitArray::with_size(self.width as usize);
356        for y in 0..self.height {
357            //for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
358            let offset = y as usize * self.row_size;
359            let rowArray = mask.getRow(y);
360            let row = rowArray.getBitArray();
361            for (x, row_x) in row.iter().enumerate().take(self.row_size) {
362                // for x in 0..self.row_size {
363                //for (int x = 0; x < rowSize; x++) {
364                self.bits[offset + x] ^= *row_x;
365            }
366        }
367        Ok(())
368    }

378    /**
379     * <p>Sets a square region of the bit matrix to true.</p>
380     *
381     * @param left The horizontal position to begin at (inclusive)
382     * @param top The vertical position to begin at (inclusive)
383     * @param width The width of the region
384     * @param height The height of the region
385     */
386    pub fn setRegion(&mut self, left: u32, top: u32, width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<()> {
387        if height < 1 || width < 1 {
388            return Err(Exceptions::illegal_argument_with(
389                "height and width must be at least 1",
390            ));
391        }
392        let right = left + width;
393        let bottom = top + height;
394        if bottom > self.height || right > self.width {
395            return Err(Exceptions::illegal_argument_with(
396                "the region must fit inside the matrix",
397            ));
398        }
399        for y in top..bottom {
400            //for (int y = top; y < bottom; y++) {
401            let offset = y as usize * self.row_size;
402            for x in left..right {
403                //for (int x = left; x < right; x++) {
404                self.bits[offset + (x as usize / BASE_BITS)] |= 1 << (x as usize & BASE_SHIFT);
405            }
406        }
407        Ok(())
408    }

410    /**
411     * A fast method to retrieve one row of data from the matrix as a BitArray.
412     *
413     * @param y The row to retrieve
414     * @param row An optional caller-allocated BitArray, will be allocated if null or too small
415     * @return The resulting BitArray - this reference should always be used even when passing
416     *         your own row
417     */
418    pub fn getRow(&self, y: u32) -> BitArray {
419        let mut rw = BitArray::with_size(self.width as usize);
420
421        let offset = y as usize * self.row_size;
422        for x in 0..self.row_size {
423            //for (int x = 0; x < rowSize; x++) {
424            rw.setBulk(x * BASE_BITS, self.bits[offset + x]);
425        }
426        rw
427    }

429    /// This method returns a column of the bitmatrix.
430    ///
431    /// The current implementation may be very slow.
432    pub fn getCol(&self, x: u32) -> BitArray {
433        let mut cw = BitArray::with_size(self.height as usize);
434
435        for y in 0..self.height {
436            if self.get(x, y) {
437                cw.set(y as usize)
438            }
439        }
440
441        cw
442    }

448    pub fn setRow(&mut self, y: u32, row: &BitArray) {
449        self.bits[y as usize * self.row_size..y as usize * self.row_size + self.row_size]
450            .clone_from_slice(&row.getBitArray()[0..self.row_size])

454    /**
455     * Modifies this {@code BitMatrix} to represent the same but rotated the given degrees (0, 90, 180, 270)
456     *
457     * @param degrees number of degrees to rotate through counter-clockwise (0, 90, 180, 270)
458     */
459    pub fn rotate(&mut self, degrees: u32) -> Result<()> {
460        match degrees % 360 {
461            0 => Ok(()),
462            90 => {
463                self.rotate90();
464                Ok(())
465            }
466            180 => {
467                self.rotate180();
468                Ok(())
469            }
470            270 => {
471                self.rotate90();
472                self.rotate180();
473                Ok(())
474            }
475            _ => Err(Exceptions::illegal_argument_with(
476                "degrees must be a multiple of 0, 90, 180, or 270",
477            )),
478        }
479    }
480
481    /**
482     * Modifies this {@code BitMatrix} to represent the same but rotated 180 degrees
483     */
484    pub fn rotate180(&mut self) {
485        // let mut topRow = BitArray::with_size(self.width as usize);
486        // let mut bottomRow = BitArray::with_size(self.width as usize);
487        let maxHeight = self.height.div_ceil(2);
488        for i in 0..maxHeight {
489            //for (int i = 0; i < maxHeight; i++) {
490            let mut topRow = self.getRow(i);
491            let bottomRowIndex = self.height - 1 - i;
492            let mut bottomRow = self.getRow(bottomRowIndex);
493            topRow.reverse();
494            bottomRow.reverse();
495            self.setRow(i, &bottomRow);
496            self.setRow(bottomRowIndex, &topRow);
497        }
498    }
499
500    /**
501     * Modifies this {@code BitMatrix} to represent the same but rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise
502     */
503    pub fn rotate90(&mut self) {
504        let newWidth = self.height;
505        let newHeight = self.width;
506        let newRowSize = newWidth.div_ceil(BASE_BITS as u32);
507        let mut newBits = vec![0; (newRowSize * newHeight) as usize];
508
509        for y in 0..self.height {
510            //for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
511            for x in 0..self.width {
512                //for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
513                let offset = self.get_offset(y, x);
514                if ((self.bits[offset] >> (x as usize & BASE_SHIFT)) & 1) != 0 {
515                    let newOffset: usize =
516                        ((newHeight - 1 - x) * newRowSize + (y / BASE_BITS as u32)) as usize;
517                    newBits[newOffset] |= 1 << (y as usize & BASE_SHIFT);
518                }
519            }
520        }
521        self.width = newWidth;
522        self.height = newHeight;
523        self.row_size = newRowSize as usize;
524        self.bits = newBits;
525    }

527    /**
528     * This is useful in detecting the enclosing rectangle of a 'pure' barcode.
529     *
530     * @return {@code left,top,width,height} enclosing rectangle of all 1 bits, or null if it is all white
531     */
532    pub fn getEnclosingRectangle(&self) -> Option<[u32; 4]> {
533        let mut left = self.width;
534        let mut top = self.height;
535        // let right = -1;
536        // let bottom = -1;
537        let mut right: u32 = 0;
538        let mut bottom = 0;
539
540        for y in 0..self.height {
541            //for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
542            for x32 in 0..self.row_size {
543                //for (int x32 = 0; x32 < rowSize; x32++) {
544                let theBits = self.bits[y as usize * self.row_size + x32];
545                if theBits != 0 {
546                    top = top.min(y);
547                    bottom = bottom.max(y);
548
549                    let bit_lo: usize = theBits.trailing_zeros() as usize;
550                    left = left.min(((x32 * BASE_BITS) + bit_lo) as u32);
551
552                    let bit_hi: usize = (BASE_BITS - 1) - (theBits.leading_zeros() as usize);
553                    right = right.max(((x32 * BASE_BITS) + bit_hi) as u32);
554                }
555            }
556        }
557
558        if right < left || bottom < top {
559            return None;
560        }
561
562        Some([left, top, right - left + 1, bottom - top + 1])
563    }
564
565    /**
566     * This is useful in detecting a corner of a 'pure' barcode.
567     *
568     * @return {@code x,y} coordinate of top-left-most 1 bit, or null if it is all white
569     */
570    pub fn getTopLeftOnBit(&self) -> Option<Point> {
571        let mut bitsOffset = 0;
572        while bitsOffset < self.bits.len() && self.bits[bitsOffset] == 0 {
573            bitsOffset += 1;
574        }
575        if bitsOffset == self.bits.len() {
576            return None;
577        }
578        let y = bitsOffset / self.row_size;
579        let mut x = (bitsOffset % self.row_size) * BASE_BITS;
580
581        let theBits = self.bits[bitsOffset];
582        let mut bit = 0;
583        while (theBits << (BASE_SHIFT - bit)) == 0 {
584            bit += 1;
585        }
586        x += bit;
587        Some(point(x as f32, y as f32))
588    }
589
590    pub fn getBottomRightOnBit(&self) -> Option<Point> {
591        let mut bitsOffset = self.bits.len() as i64 - 1;
592        while bitsOffset >= 0 && self.bits[bitsOffset as usize] == 0 {
593            bitsOffset -= 1;
594        }
595        if bitsOffset < 0 {
596            return None;
597        }
598
599        let y = bitsOffset as usize / self.row_size;
600        let mut x = (bitsOffset as usize % self.row_size) * BASE_BITS;
601
602        let theBits = self.bits[bitsOffset as usize];
603        let mut bit = BASE_BITS - 1;
604        while (theBits >> bit) == 0 {
605            bit -= 1;
606        }
607        x += bit;
608
609        Some(point(x as f32, y as f32))
610    }

675    /**
676     * @param setString representation of a set bit
677     * @param unsetString representation of an unset bit
678     * @param lineSeparator newline character in string representation
679     * @return string representation of entire matrix utilizing given strings and line separator
680     * @deprecated call {@link #toString(String,String)} only, which uses \n line separator always
681     */
682    fn buildToString(&self, setString: &str, unsetString: &str, lineSeparator: &str) -> String {
683        let mut result =
684            String::with_capacity((self.height * (self.width + 1)).try_into().unwrap());
685        for y in 0..self.height {
686            //for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
687            for x in 0..self.width {
688                //for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
689                result.push_str(if self.get(x, y) {
690                    setString
691                } else {
692                    unsetString
693                });
694            }
695            result.push_str(lineSeparator);
696        }
697        result
698    }

705    //     let area = self.bits.iter().skip(self.row_size * top).take(self.row_size * height)
706    //     .copied().collect::<Vec<u32>>();
707    //     let new_bits = area.chunks(self.row_size)
708    //     .skip(left).take(width).flatten().copied().collect::<Vec<u32>>();
709    //     Self { width: width, height: height, row_size: width, bits: () }
710    // }
711    pub fn crop(&self, top: usize, left: usize, height: usize, width: usize) -> BitMatrix {
712        let mut new_bm = BitMatrix::new(width as u32, height as u32).expect("create empty");
713        for y in top..top + height {
714            // let row = self.getRow(y as u32);
715            for x in left..left + width {
716                if self.get(x as u32, y as u32) {
717                    new_bm.set(x as u32, y as u32)
718                }
719            }
720        }
721        new_bm
722    }

724    #[inline(always)]
725    pub fn is_in(&self, p: Point) -> bool {
726        self.isIn(p, 0)
727    }
728
729    #[inline(always)]
730    pub fn isIn(&self, p: Point, b: i32) -> bool {
731        b as f32 <= p.x
732            && p.x < self.getWidth() as f32 - b as f32
733            && b as f32 <= p.y
734            && p.y < self.getHeight() as f32 - b as f32
735    }
736}

746
747    fn try_from(value: &str) -> std::prelude::v1::Result<Self, Self::Error> {
748        Self::parse_strings(value, "X", " ")

752impl From<&BitMatrix> for Vec<bool> {
753    fn from(value: &BitMatrix) -> Self {
754        let mut arr = vec![false; (value.width * value.height) as usize];
755        for x in 0..value.width {
756            for y in 0..value.height {
757                let insert_pos = ((y * value.width) + x) as usize;
758                arr[insert_pos] = value.get(x, y);
759            }
760        }
761        arr
762    }
763}

765#[cfg(feature = "image")]
766/// This should only be used if you *know* that the `DynamicImage` is binary.
767impl TryFrom<image::DynamicImage> for BitMatrix {
768    type Error = Exceptions;
769
770    fn try_from(value: image::DynamicImage) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
771        let mut new_bitmatrix = BitMatrix::new(value.width(), value.height())?;
772        for (x, y, value) in value.as_luma8().unwrap().enumerate_pixels() {
773            if value.0[0] != u8::MAX {
774                new_bitmatrix.set(x, y)
775            }
776        }
777        Ok(new_bitmatrix)
778    }
779}

788#[cfg(feature = "image")]
789impl From<&BitMatrix> for image::DynamicImage {
790    fn from(value: &BitMatrix) -> Self {
791        let mut pixels = image::ImageBuffer::new(value.width, value.height);
792
793        for (x, y, pixel) in pixels.enumerate_pixels_mut() {
794            let new_pixel = if value.get(x, y) {
795                image::Rgb([0, 0, 0])
796            } else {
797                image::Rgb([u8::MAX, u8::MAX, u8::MAX])
798            };
799            *pixel = new_pixel
800        }
801
802        pixels.into()
803    }
804}

806#[cfg(feature = "svg_write")]
807impl From<&BitMatrix> for svg::Document {
808    fn from(value: &BitMatrix) -> Self {
809        let block_size = 1;
810        let mut document = svg::Document::new().set(
811            "viewBox",
812            (0, 0, value.width * block_size, value.height * block_size),
813        );
814        for x in 0..value.width {
815            for y in 0..value.height {
816                if value.get(x, y) {
817                    let block = svg::node::element::Rectangle::new()
818                        .set("x", x * block_size)
819                        .set("y", y * block_size)
820                        .set("width", block_size)
821                        .set("height", block_size);
822                    document = document.add(block);
823                }
824            }
825        }
826        document
827    }
828}
